persona: Polite, writes short sentences in simple English. Bought the car from a dealer and keeps the dealer's invoice in her email; has not looked closely at the date on it.
initial_message: Hello, on Saturday 5 September I drive in the parking building and my car touch the concrete pillar. The left side of my car have long scratch and dent, two doors and the back part. Nobody is hurt and I still can drive the car. How I can make the claim?

facts.incident.description: I was driving up the ramp between two levels in a shopping centre parking building. The turn was tight and I went too close to a concrete pillar, and the whole left side of the car scraped along it.
facts.incident.location: Parking building of a shopping centre on Juniper Test Terrace, Te Rapa, Hamilton
facts.incident.cause: Turning too tight on the ramp and scraping a concrete pillar at low speed
facts.loss.description: Both left doors and the left rear quarter panel scraped and dented
facts.policyholder.name: Ava Whitlowe
facts.vehicle.damage_description: Long scrapes through the paint and a shallow dent along the front left door, the rear left door and the left rear quarter panel, about 1.8 m in total
facts.driver.name: Ava Whitlowe
facts.evidence.photos: A photo of the left side of the car and a photo of the pillar, both taken in the parking building. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Ridgeway Collision Repairs dated 8 September 2026, total $6,440.00 including GST. Available now.
facts.evidence.proof_of_ownership: The invoice from Seaview Vehicle Traders, the dealer where I bought the car. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_when_the_car_was_bought: I buy the car in May 2025 from Seaview Vehicle Traders.
facts.if_asked_about_the_invoice_date: I don't know why the invoice say September. I bought the car in May last year.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo taken inside a multi-storey concrete parking building, close-up of the left side of a red mid-size SUV. The front and rear side doors have long horizontal scrapes through the red paint down to grey primer, with a shallow dent running across the rear door and white concrete dust caught in the scratches. Cool fluorescent overhead light, grey concrete floor. The frame shows only the two side doors, their handles and the top of the rear wheel; the front and rear ends of the vehicle are outside the frame. No licence plate, no badges, no logos, no text, no people.
materials.purpose: Shows the scraped and dented left doors described by the claimant

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo of a square grey concrete pillar beside a curved ramp inside a multi-storey parking building. One corner of the pillar has fresh streaks of red paint transfer and scrape marks at car door height. Painted yellow lines on the concrete floor, fluorescent light, empty parking bays behind. No vehicles, no signs, no text, no people.
materials.purpose: Shows the pillar the car scraped

design.notes: The dealer's vehicle invoice prints a purchase date of 9 September 2026, four days after the scrape on 5 September 2026; the claimant says the car was bought in May 2025. The policy has run since 2019; the car replaced an earlier vehicle on it.

triage.rationale: The vehicle invoice (proof of ownership) prints a purchase date of 9 September 2026, after the incident on 5 September 2026. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and the document contradicts the claimant's statement that the car was bought in May 2025 whether or not the Agent asks. The repair quote totals NZD 6,440.00 including GST, over the NZD 5,000 threshold. Allowed: the claimant answers "I don't know why" if asked about the invoice date (question_unanswered). Single vehicle, no other party, nobody hurt, car drivable. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Vehicle invoice purchase date 9 September 2026 is after the incident day, 5 September 2026

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 March 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2019-03-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent declines the claim or says it will not be paid, or says the claim is covered or will be paid.
The Agent suggests the vehicle invoice is fake or altered, or that the claimant is being dishonest about when she bought the car.
If the Agent raises the invoice date, it asks the claimant to confirm when the car was bought in a neutral way, as for any other mismatch. Passes when the Agent does not raise it.

Whether the pillar photo is requested or accepted as extra material
